opportunities.title: Generative AI for Small Business
opportunities.description: Join us online with Digital Main Street. As AI continues to evolve, how your business utilizes it for your online presence can also evolve your brand. In this webinar, you will learn about generative AI and the different ways it can help your business. The webinar will discuss best practices for applying it to your marketing strategies, various AI platforms, and the areas it can support your business. Attendees will walk away with a solid understanding of generative AI and how to integrate it with their existing marketing plans. GenAI Tools being explored: 1. Gemini 2. Gemini Notebook 3. Nano Banana Session Agenda: 1. What is Generative AI? 2. AI & Your Daily Operations 3. AI & Customer Support 4. AI & Marketing 5. Best Practices for AI: Challenges with Using AI and How to Mitigate Them This program is part of the Newcomer Entrepreneurship Initiative and our continued efforts to champion inclusive entrepreneurship in Toronto, by finding more ways to uplift and support the journeys of diverse entrepreneurial communities such as newcomer entrepreneurs, Black entrepreneurs, and women entrepreneurs. We strive to accomplish this through storytelling, shared experiences, and open conversations that reflect the diversity of Toronto’s small business community. Registration: This virtual Zoom event is free to join. Once registered, you’ll receive an email with the Zoom link. Need help with Zoom? - Joining and participating in a Zoom webinar - Zoom Privacy Statement Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Resilience Reads: a climate neighbourhood reading party
opportunities.description: Join us to share the joy of reading, while building climate resilience knowledge. Members are invited to discuss a book they are reading, tell stories, and empower each other to explore community-driven solutions. Each party will start with a quiet read and reflect time, with opportunities to join group discussions later on over refreshments. AUGUST – Fossil Fuel Folly American War by Omar El Akkad or your favourite dystopian read! or your favourite book featuring water! SEPTEMBER – We Need Pollinators The History of Bees by Maja Lunde or your favourite animal-centred book! OCTOBER – Climate Change is Scary The Annual Migration of Clouds by Premee Mohamed or a different book that shares a scary future ecological crisis! NOVEMBER - Climate Changes Everything Ministry for the Future by Kim Stanley Robinson or your favourite time travel read! Copies are available in the branch to pick up, while supplies last. Registration is encouraged but drop ins are welcome! Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Python Essentials 2 Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Take an intermediate Python course to advance your programming skills. This learning circle will meet online on Thursday afternoons, 2-3:30pm for August 6 to September 24. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly to complete the course together. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions. Python Essentials 2 is designed for learners who are already familiar with the essentials of Python, including programming concepts like data types, containers, functions, conditions, and loops. Required: completion of the Python Essentials 1 course, or equivalent experience. Python Essentials 2 is the second in a 2-course series that will prepare you for the PCAP – Certified Associate in Python Programming certification exam at Pearson VUE. This intermediate-level course covers advanced aspects of Python programming , including modules, packages, exceptions, file processing, as well as general coding techniques and object-oriented programming (OOP). For more information about the Python Essentials 2 learning circle, please contact networkingacademy@tpl.ca Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.description: Build on your basic Microsoft Word skills and learn to use Word more effectively. In this class, you will: Practice new Word skills while you design a flyer Format text, margins, indents, headers and footers Format text as columns Create bulleted, numbered and sorted lists Review your document with Spelling and Grammar check and Thesaurus Upon completion of this class, you will be able to use even more Word tools to design your documents. Prerequisites: Word Basics 1 or equivalent skills. Basic keyboarding and mouse skills required. Format: Hands-on with demonstrations Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. opportunities.description: It’s always a good day to observe birds in your garden, from the snowy depths of winter to the height of summer bloom. In this program presented by the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority, learn about common nesting, wintering, and migratory birds in the Greater Toronto Area, and how to attract, feed, and observe them throughout the seasons! This program is part of Youth Hub service. Youth Hubs are a welcoming place for teens after school and in the summer, where helpful staff are always available. Free, nutritious snacks are offered daily. Drop by a branch with a Youth Hub or call the branch to find out more.

opportunities.title: Make your own Fidget Spinner
opportunities.description: Get ready to spin, design, and create in this hands-on 3D workshop for kids aged 6–12! Young creators will step into the shoes of an engineer to design their own custom fidget spinner. They will use Tinkercad , a beginner-friendly 3D modeling platform. During the session, kids will learn basic spatial skills and shape manipulation. They will also explore the mechanics of motion to bring their unique ideas to life. Every participant walks away with a digital blueprint ready to turn into a real, high-speed toy! Participants will be able to pick up their 3D printed fidget at a later date for free . Only one 3D printed fidget spinner per person. Aged 6–12!

opportunities.title: Data Analytics Essentials Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space! A learning circle is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment. Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field. In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to: transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel query data from a relational database using SQL improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau We will meet online every Thursday evening, September 24 - December 10, 6-7:30 PM (12 sessions). Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend sessions on a weekly basis. Learners who complete the course will be able to: earn a digital badge download a certificate of completion

opportunities.title: Google AI Essentials: In Person Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization. This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz. By completing the specialization, you will learn: How AI works How to write effective prompts How to use generative AI tools responsibly How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm How to stay up to date with AI news After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions. No AI experience is required. How to Join a Learning Circle: Register once on the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address . A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions in person at Northern District Branch . Registration is a two-step procedure. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.description: Curious about the Cricut? In this introductory class, participants will explore the creative possibilities of this popular cutting machine. You’ll also see a demonstration of the machine in action, showing how easy it is to design and cut custom creations. Perfect for anyone looking to get started with the Cricut and learn more about how you can use the Cricut in our makerspace!

opportunities.title: Shedding light on the dark side of the Universe
opportunities.description: The standard model of cosmology tells us that the Universe is mostly made up of ‘Dark Matter’, with normal matter contributing only about 15% of the total budget. However, direct detections have not yielded any results about the nature of this mysterious dark matter, leaving us with only indirect means of inferring its existence and distribution. I will try to answer tantalizing questions about its nature, and how it may have helped shape the Universe. Presenter: Pratika Dayal Special thanks to the Dunlap Institute for Astronomy & Astrophysics at the University of Toronto.
opportunities.address: St. Lawrence, 171 Front Street East, Toronto, ON, M5A 4H3

opportunities.title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles! What You'll Learn This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover: Essential Prompting Skills : How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results. Everyday Work Tasks: Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more. Data & Presentations: How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data. Advanced Techniques: How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time. Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions. Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle. How to Joi n a Learning Circle: Register once for the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address. A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions online via Zoom, Friday September 11, 18, 25 and Oct 2, from 1:30-4PM. Registration is a two-step process. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: 3D Design with Onshape
opportunities.description: Learn how to create parametric designs using cloud based software Onshape. This hands-on workshop introduces participants to the fundamentals of 3D design using Onshape, a cloud-based CAD software. Whether you're an aspiring engineer, designer, or hobbyist, this session provides the tools and knowledge to start creating your own 3D models. What You’ll Learn: Getting Started: Overview of Onshape's interface, navigation tools, and cloud-based collaboration features. Core Design Principles: Understanding 3D modeling basics, including sketches, extrusions, and revolutions. Hands-On Practice: Creating simple 3D parts, assembling components, and exploring design modifications. Best Practices: Tips for efficient modeling, managing design iterations, and exporting models for 3D printing or other applications. This program is ideal for beginners with no prior experience in CAD software, as well as those looking to explore Onshape's capabilities. Registration will start 2 weeks before this class. Computers will be provided. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. opportunities.description: If you've ever wanted to up your photography game, whether you just want to get better at taking pictures with your phone, or you want to graduate to a professional DSLR or mirrorless camera, join us for a class on the basics of photography. We will go over the basic settings that go into a good photo as well as talking about camera settings, lenses, and lighting. Registration opens 2 weeks prior to class. All equipment will be provided. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). opportunities.title: After School Club
opportunities.description: Looking for something to do after school? Come out to our After School Club and learn new things, make stuff, meet other kids and have fun! For ages 6 to 8 year. Want to play with electricity? Turn on a light, spin a motor, activate a speaker; work your way through the 100+ circuitry projects as you learn about electricity! Join us for a fun-filled After School Club Snap Circuit program series on September. Registrar all two programs in the series online or call us. Friday, September 18th: Snap Circuit 1 & 2 Friday, September 25th: Snap Circuit 3 & 4 Snacks are offered during the After School Club for participants. Ingredient lists will be available. Snacks are generously supported, in part, by donors. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Excel Basics 3: PivotTables & Conditional Formatting
opportunities.description: Build on your basic Microsoft Excel skills and learn to use Excel data effectively. In this third session, you will: Use Conditional Formatting to visualize data Explore the power of PivotTables for data summary and analysis Sort and filter the data in tables and using slicers Take home practice data to improve your new skills Upon completion of this class, you will be able to get more from your data using Pivot tables. Prerequisites: Excel Basics 1 and 2 or equivalent knowledge. Basic mouse and keyboard skills required. Format: Hands-on with demonstrations Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: (九月專題：新學期，新起點！新移民家庭的「開學收心指南」) Back-to-School Reset – Building Healthy Routines and Digital Habits
opportunities.description: Join Family Services York Region for a practical Back-to-School Reset! This session is facilitated in Mandarin and is perfect for newcomer families. Gain tools for smoother transitions and balanced tech use. Participants will learn: How to establish healthy family routines. How to manage screen time. How to build positive digital habits that support your child’s success in schools. 開學了，如何幫助孩子收心？ 總是為了手機、電腦和孩子吵架？ 誠邀您參加 「 開學收心指南」實用講座！ 一起解鎖健康家庭作息、合理控管螢幕時間，培養健康的電子產品使用習慣。 *The program's facilitator also speaks Cantonese*
opportunities.address: Milliken Mills Branch, 7600 Kennedy Road, Unit 1, Markham, Ontario, L3R 9S5

opportunities.title: L'univers sombre et magnifique
opportunities.description: Depuis des millénaires, les êtres humains contemplent le ciel nocturne et s'interrogent sur l'origine de l'univers. D'où vient-il ? De quoi est-ce fait? Où va-t-il? Dans cette présentation, Renée Hložek vous parlerai de cet univers — à la fois sombre et magnifique — et de la manière dont nous utilisons les télescopes pour en percer les secrets. Renée Hložek est cosmologiste sud-africaine et professeure agrégée au Dunlap Institute for Astronomy & Astrophysics de l’Université de Toronto. Ses recherches portent sur les origines et l’évolution de l’Univers, notamment le fond diffus cosmologique, l’énergie noire et la matière noire. Elle participe à d’importantes collaborations internationales, telles que l’Atacama Cosmology Telescope, le Simons Observatory et le Vera C. Rubin Observatory. Elle a reçu la médaille du roi Charles III pour la communication d’idées scientifiques, ainsi que la médaille Rutherford et la bourse Arthur B. McDonald du Conseil de recherches en sciences naturelles et en génie du Canada. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8. ACCESSIBILITÉ Le sous-titrage en direct ou automatique, l’interprétation en langue des signes, les services d’intervenant, ou les services d’accompagnement sont disponibles sur demande. Veuillez soumettre votre demande au moins deux semaines à l’avance à : tpl.ca/accessibility-events .

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Passive Worksheets (Wordsearches & Colouring) + Kapla Blocks & Challenge Cards + Guest Speaker Day speaker from City of Markham's Environmental Services, 11am-12 noon PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Markham Village
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity
opportunities.description: Want to learn how to add custom audio to your films and videos? Perhaps a voiceover? Join us in our Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity workshop! Audacity is an easy-to-use, multi-track audio editor and recorder for Windows, macOS, GNU/Linux and other operating systems. Audacity is a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) that is FREE to download. This makerspace demonstration will provide instruction on how to use this program to get you started with sound editing and recording. We will cover how to edit sound, what effects this program has to offer on your vocals and how to mix down your different tracks. At the end of the session you will receive a quick tour of Markham Village's sound booth and more information on how to book the space. With your new skills, why not participate in our upcoming Markham Village Film Festival ? Hope to see you there. Become Maker Certified Please note: if you are looking to use our makerspaces independently, you must be 13+ and complete this online Makerspace module . Once completed, our staff can update your profile and you will be maker certified!
opportunities.address: Markham Village Branch, 6031 Highway 7, Markham, Ontario, L3P 3A7

opportunities.title: Digitizing & Restoring 35mm Slides with AI
opportunities.description: Learn how to preserve your memories by converting 35mm slides or negatives into high resolution digital images. This demonstration introduces the process of scanning 35mm slides, and AI-powered restoration/modification techniques to remove deterioration and correcting the images' colours. Participants will leave with the knowledge needed to begin digitizing and restoring their own slide collections. Learning outcomes: Learn how to scan and digitize 35mm slides (or negatives) using Makerspace equipment Use AI tools to enhance scanned images by correcting colour and removing common imperfections Note: Program may allow drop-in participants, if space allows. Become Maker Certified Please note: if you are looking to use our makerspaces independently, you must be 13+ and complete this online Makerspace module . Once completed, our staff can update your profile and you will be maker certified!

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Thornhill Community Centre
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.description: Join our G1-G2 level Tips and Fun with Math virtually, where students can sit comfortably at home while receiving classroom quality math deliverables, develop basic logic and arithmetic skills, a general understanding of geometry, and practice simple word problems! opportunities.title: Discover a Career in Science/Health Care
opportunities.description: Are you interested in starting a career in the field of health care? Or perhaps you work in the health care field and are looking to add to your education to move into a new area of health care? We’ll highlight important things such as: We will cover programs such as Personal Support Worker, Practical Nursing, Registered Nursing and Medical Device Reprocessing We will cover programs in the field of Science We will touch on entrance requirements, steps to apply A bit about financial aid and student supports **Please note: This workshop is run in partnership with Seneca Polytechnic**. _______ Registrants will receive an email with the Zoom link 1 day prior to the program. If you do not receive the Zoom link the day before the program: Check your email inbox and spam folders. If you still cannot find the email, please contact us at mplcommunitylibrarians@markhamlibrary.ca prior to the program start time so we can provide you with the link.
opportunities.address: Markham Village Branch, 6031 Highway 7, Markham, Ontario, L3P 3A7

opportunities.title: Be An Active Digital Citizen - Play-based Workshop for Families
opportunities.description: In this play-based, interactive workshop for children and families, we explore what it means to be a smart, safe, and empowered digital citizen. Through games and hands-on activities, children will practice healthy social media habits and learn about their digital rights online in a fun, age-appropriate way. At the end of this workshop, participants should: Be able to recognize healthy vs. unhealthy social media habits and practice simple strategies for balanced use. Understand basic digital rights for children online (i.e. privacy, safety, expression). Build confidence identifying safe, respectful ways to engage with others online, both individually and as a family. Note: this session is intended to be intended by families including children aged 8 - 16 and their parents/caregivers . Please register for each individual attending. Hosted by Kids Rights Canada .

opportunities.title: CyberSafe Seniors, Preventing AI Fraud and Scams
opportunities.description: CyberSafe Seniors, Preventing AI Fraud and Scams which addresses the growing threat of AI-enabled online fraud and scams targeting older Canadians. As AI tools become more accessible, scammers are using tactics such as voice cloning, deepfake videos, and highly convincing phishing techniques to impersonate loved ones and fabricate financial emergencies. Older adults aged 55+ are disproportionately targeted, often experiencing significant financial loss along with shame, anxiety, and social isolation. Through workshops delivered by MediaSmarts experts participants will learn how AI-enabled scams work, how to verify messages from family or financial institutions, and what steps to take if targeted.

Note: There will be a hands-on component to this program so we highly recommend bringing a laptop or mobile device so you can try out what we've talked about on your own!

opportunities.title: How We Stay Relevant in the Age of AI
opportunities.description: AI is changing how people think about work, learning, and human value. Many professionals, parents, students, and community members are asking a very real question: if AI can generate answers, summaries, explanations, drafts, code, and ideas so quickly, where do humans remain relevant? This session argues that humans should not try to compete with AI at speed, recall, or routine output. That is the wrong competition. As AI makes answers easier to produce, human value moves toward deeper understanding, disciplined curiosity, judgment, and the ability to question, verify, and ground what AI produces. For most of us, learning has often been treated as natural and implicit. We were taught subjects in school, but not always taught how learning itself works. Machine learning gives us a useful mirror. In order to teach machines how to learn, humans had to make parts of learning explicit: objectives, data, patterns, prediction, feedback, error correction, validation, calibration, and updating. This session uses those machine learning principles not as a technical lesson, but as a way to think about how humans can learn more deeply in the age of AI. Participants will explore why superficial knowledge is becoming less survivable, why AI still needs to be grounded in human reality, and how disciplined curiosity can help people remain valuable as AI becomes more capable. The session will include a short lecture-style presentation followed by a guided audience discussion. The discussion can be shaped around a small number of reflection questions, with flexibility to shift into Q&A or a brief example/demo depending on the audience engagement and MPL’s preference. No technical background is required. By the end of this session, participants will be able to: Explain why shallow learning and routine knowledge work become more vulnerable when AI can generate fluent answers quickly. Apply key machine learning principles, such as objective-setting, feedback, error correction, validation, calibration, and updating, as a practical framework for deeper human learning, better questioning, and stronger judgment. Bio: Darren Soo is a Canadian technology founder and creator of PI, an individualized AI reasoning framework designed to help people reason through complex, changing information over time. His background spans more than two decades of practical technology work across enterprise and operational software environments. His current work centres on artificial intelligence, machine learning, and explainable reasoning systems, while his broader interests include how technology can support curiosity, better questions, learning and decision-making.

opportunities.title: Vibe Coding: Create Programs and Apps using AI
opportunities.description: "Vibe Coding" is a coding approach that uses AI as your programming partner—no coding knowledge required! Using vibe coding, you can create apps, websites, and simple language simply by describing what you want. In this hands-on session, you'll learn to describe in simple language what you want and let the AI help create the code. You don't need any prior programming skills or experience at all! This is the perfect introduction to coding in the age of AI... all you need is curiosity and creativity! Note: There will be a hands-on component to this program so we highly recommend bringing a laptop or mobile device so you can try out what we've talked about on your own!

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Aaniin
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.title: AI Powered Job Search
opportunities.description: Are you using AI in your job search journey? Learn how to use AI to make your job search easier and more effective. In this workshop, you'll discover how AI can help you improve your resume, tailor it for Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), find jobs that match your skills, prepare for interviews, research employers, and stay organized throughout your job search. You'll also learn how to use AI safely and responsibly, with practical tips and prompts you can start using right away. No experience with AI is required. Learning outcomes: - discover how AI can help you improve your resume - discover how AI can help you with your whole job searching journey - learn how to use AI safely and responsibly in your job searching journey Presenter's bio: This workshop is facilitated by VPI Employment Services. Since 1988, VPI Employment Services have been delivering employment services to help individuals, employers, and communities achieve their goals at no cost . Their work focuses on providing tailored employment programs, vocational assessments, and supportive services to jobseekers that help build job readiness, provide access to training, and connect them with meaningful and sustainable employment opportunities.

opportunities.title: Creative Writing in the AI Apocalypse: Community Conversation with Joseph Donato
opportunities.description: How will writers survive the age of Artificial Intelligence?” Everyone’s got a story to tell, but the threat generative AI poses on the creative arts may discourage writers from putting pen to paper. Join this Community Conversation to understand the role of writers today, share your opinions on creative writing in an AI world, and engage with some related writing prompts. Joseph Donato is a Queer writer, editor, and library worker. He has completed his MFA in Creative Writing at the University of Guelph, and his most recent poetry chapbook, No One Should Be Happy When I'm Not was published in 2026. Joseph's poems have appeared in The Ampersand Review, Pinhole Magazine, and more. He enjoys dad rock, money, and being afraid. He can be found @josephdonato13 on Instagram or josephdonato.ca .

opportunities.description: Gather beneath the harvest moon and celebrate with MPL! Inspired by cultural traditions from around the world, our Moon & Harvest Festival honours the season of abundance, the beauty of the full moon, and the joy of coming together as a community. 🌕🏮🍂✨ Enjoy free family-friendly activities, crafts, interactive experiences, and festive fun! Activities will include: Scavenger Hunt & Themed Crafts Korean Hanbok Fashion Show presented by Seshil Hanbok (6:15pm) Bake Code Mooncake Display (and free samples!) Traditional Knot Making Craft Royal Astronomical Society of Canada's Telescope Display Lantern Craft Workshop (1) 5:30-6:00pm (Register here) Lantern Craft Workshop (2) 6:30-7:00pm (Register here) Lastly, heartwarming reunions are a must 🧡 We look forward to welcoming you there! **NOTE:
